questions.q: What do SQL Server statistics actually represent?
options: A histogram-like summary of data distribution the optimizer uses to estimate row counts
A physical copy of every row in the table
A list of every index on a table
A security audit log
questions.explain: Statistics summarize data distribution, letting the optimizer estimate how many rows a predicate will match and choose a plan accordingly.

questions.q: What does UPDATE STATISTICS dbo.Orders WITH FULLSCAN do differently from the default?
options: It reads every row instead of a sample, more accurate but more expensive
It only updates statistics on indexed columns
It disables auto-update statistics permanently
It rebuilds the underlying indexes as well
questions.explain: The default UPDATE STATISTICS uses a sampled scan; FULLSCAN reads every row, trading cost for accuracy.

questions.q: What is a key limitation of sp_updatestats compared to a targeted UPDATE STATISTICS ... WITH FULLSCAN?
options: It always uses a sampled scan and never performs a full scan
It cannot be scheduled as an Agent job
It updates statistics on every table regardless of whether they changed
It requires sysadmin permissions that UPDATE STATISTICS does not
questions.explain: sp_updatestats is a convenient database-wide sweep, but it always samples — it's not a substitute for a targeted full-scan update where accuracy really matters.

questions.q: Why do high-churn OLTP tables need a scheduled statistics update rather than relying solely on AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS?
options: The auto-update threshold is percentage-based and can lag behind how fast a heavily-churning table's data distribution actually shifts
AUTO_UPDATE_STATISTICS only works on read-only databases
High-churn tables cannot have statistics at all
Scheduled jobs are required by SQL Server for any OLTP table
questions.explain: The auto-update trigger is a percentage of rows changed; a huge, constantly-churning table can go a long time between auto-triggered updates relative to how quickly its real distribution shifts.

questions.q: What should happen to statistics immediately after a large bulk load, per this lesson's guidance?
options: They should be updated explicitly right away, regardless of the regular schedule
Nothing — auto-update always handles bulk loads instantly
The table should be dropped and recreated
Statistics should be disabled on that table going forward
questions.explain: A large bulk load can shift data distribution enough that the optimizer's next plans are visibly wrong until statistics are explicitly refreshed.
